evidence: Built a real bare remote, a producer clone and a separate controller clone, then injected four push-boundary fault classes (python3 -I push_boundary_injector.py, exit 1) and ran 11 unittest cases (python3 -I -m unittest discover, 11 tests OK). Observed: a pre-push failure left the commit absent from the remote and ingestion returned RECOVERY_REQUIRED while the 53 committed bytes stayed byte-identical in the producer clone; a pushed result that the controller had already fetched was ingested to PARENT_INGESTED with zero errors and a matching read-back; a pushed result that the controller had not fetched was verified present on the remote yet still returned RECOVERY_REQUIRED because ingest_result runs git cat-file only in the coordinator's own repository and never fetches; after normalising object ids and task names the pre-push and pushed-but-unfetched error signatures were byte-identical, so the two failure modes are indistinguishable to the mechanism. A rejected non-fast-forward push left the competing worker's commit as the remote tip and the producer's bytes intact. false_completions_observed was 0 across all four classes. The hypothesis is refuted on both clauses that matter: the failures are not distinguishable, and a pushed-but-unreported result is not recovered. The repair candidate repair_candidate_remote_recovery.py classifies PRESENT_LOCALLY / PRESENT_ON_REMOTE_NOT_FETCHED / ABSENT_EVERYWHERE by asking the remote, then fetches and re-ingests through the unmodified ingest_result; its tests show PARENT_INGESTED for the pushed case, refusal for the absent case, and no COMPLETED state ever set.
falsifiable_hypothesis: A failure before or after push is distinguishable and recoverable, and a pushed-but-unreported result is not lost.
limitations: The remote is a local bare repository, so no network partition, authentication failure or partial-transfer condition was exercised; only the object-availability boundary was.

The pushed-but-unreported result is durable in the remote object store; the failure is in the recovery path, not in git, and the defect tests will fail by design once a coordinator adopts the repair candidate.
provider_run_id is NOT_SUPPORTED because this runtime exposes no subagent spawn tool and therefore no separate provider run identifier.
